analysis.evidence: מִלְחָמָה means “war” and is the object of עָשׂוּ. Together they mean “they waged war.” The kings listed after אֶת are their opponents.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: עָשׂוּ מִלְחָמָה means “they waged war.” The verse names Bera of Sodom and the other kings as their opponents. This rules out the source gloss “underworld.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no attached prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עָשׂוּ מִלְחָמָה אֶת בֶּרַע, the kings waged war against Bera. The parallel וְאֶת בִּרְשַׁע names Birsha as another opponent.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition with no prefix or pronominal suffix.
